stepNotes.1: The adapter boundary spans provider definitions, process orchestration, attachment materialization, prompt conversion, parsing, probing, and model resolution.
stepNotes.2: Prompt data, files, environment values, workspace access, and untrusted child output cross the subprocess boundary; argv construction and environment sanitization reduce exposure.
stepNotes.3: Generate and stream paths coordinate aborts, exits, pipe completion, cleanup, and empty-output errors; stdin listeners are installed before any write.
stepNotes.4: JSONL parsing has a non-JSON fast path and UTF-8 decoder, while generation buffers full output and streaming uses a resettable inactivity ceiling.
stepNotes.5: Wire parsing and provider policy are separated from the loader registry, though provider-ID tables must remain synchronized across three focused files.
stepNotes.6: Invalid encodings and absent instance context have explicit fallbacks; only best-effort temp cleanup suppresses its own failure, and no stale marker was found.
stepNotes.7: Seven focused files cover 116 cases across process lifecycle, parsing, prompts, attachments, probes, and resolution; streaming EPIPE remains a useful additive case.
stepNotes.8: The sole Critical record remains verified-fixed after a second source and regression-test pass; no new invariant breach was established.
stepNotes.9: All 116 focused tests, the isolated stdin EPIPE regression, and the core package typecheck passed on 2026-08-11.
